newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama bolsa to act against money laundering.
newsitem.headline: Panama bolsa to act against money laundering.

text.p: Panama's Congress plans to revamp the stock exchange law next year to modernize the system and prevent money laundering, a top lawmaker said Thursday.

Alberto Aleman Boyd, president of the congressional drug committee and a member of the ruling Democratic Revolutionary Party, said the bolsa was vulnerable to money laundering therefore the 20-year-old stock exchange law should be changed.

He explained to reporters that "someone from Peru can deposit $250,000 cash in a national bank in the name of a business from the free-trade zone ... With a check they can buy stock. The check from the bank legitimizes the money."
Speaking at a meeting with members of Panama's Stock Brokers Association, Aleman said his committee would like "to establish new parameters to minimize the illicit use of money."
Brokers Association president Dulcidio de la Guardia welcomed the possible changes.

"We need a new law that improves the whole picture. The actual law ... only addresses offerings to the public in the primary market. It doesn't address problems of secondary market transactions," he said.
De la Guardia said the association also recommended that the government changed the way it issues bonds, saying they were subject to theft and money laundering.
"Government securities are bearer, and we've had some problems in the market with bearer securities. They can be stolen, falsified and used for money laundering," he said.
